intro_notes: NOTE: Choose THREE groups that have different racial, cultural, national, or ethnic backgrounds, one of which comes from your own background. Use these groups to meet requirements 1, 2, and 3.
NOTE: The official merit badge pamphlets are now free and downloadable HERE or can be purchased at the Scout Shop.

requirements.lead_text: Do TWO of the following, choosing a different group for each:
requirements.req_text: Do TWO of the following, choosing a different group for each: (a) Go to a festival, celebration, or other event identified with one of the groups. Report on what you see and learn. (b) Go to a place of worship, school, or other institution identified with one of the groups. Report on what you see and learn. (c) Talk with a person from one of the groups about the heritage and traditions of the group. Report on what you learn. (d) Learn a song, dance, poem, or story that is traditional to one group, and teach it to a group of your friends. (e) Go to a library or museum to see a program or exhibit featuring one group's traditions. Report on what you see and learn.

Observing Storyteller Expressions: He listens closely and watches the storytellers' expressions and movements (p. 31).
Audience Engagement Techniques: Their techniques will help him entertain his own audiences (p. 31).
Historical Origins of Folk tales: During a break, Nate asks the storytellers about the history behind the old stories, when the tales were written or performed in the native country (p. 31).
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 - Practice Audience Delivery Techniques: Their techniques will help him entertain his own audiences (p. 31).
Step 2 - Ask About Story Origins: During a break, Nate asks the storytellers about the history behind the old stories, when the tales were written or performed in the native country (p. 31).
Step 3 - Trace Generational Oral Traditions: They have been handed down through the generations, and no one knows just how they began (p. 31).
Step 4 - Identify Event Specific Traditions: He also learns that some traditional stories are told only at certain events or celebrations (p. 31).

quiz_item.scenario_prompt: When comparing three different cultural groups in the United States for Requirement 1, what is the primary goal of examining their traditions, customs, and historical contributions?
quiz_item.question: When comparing three different cultural groups in the United States for Requirement 1, what is the primary goal of examining their traditions, customs, and historical contributions?
options: A. To understand how diverse cultural backgrounds shape American society, build mutual respect, and recognize shared human values alongside distinct heritages.
B. To rank cultural groups by the century they arrived in North America and determine which group should set uniform national customs.
C. To prove that regional differences in language, food, and holidays have completely disappeared in modern metropolitan areas.
D. To replace local cultural celebrations with a single standardized set of civic traditions across all states.
choices: A. To understand how diverse cultural backgrounds shape American society, build mutual respect, and recognize shared human values alongside distinct heritages.
B. To rank cultural groups by the century they arrived in North America and determine which group should set uniform national customs.
C. To prove that regional differences in language, food, and holidays have completely disappeared in modern metropolitan areas.
D. To replace local cultural celebrations with a single standardized set of civic traditions across all states.
quiz_item.correct_answer: A. To understand how diverse cultural backgrounds shape American society, build mutual respect, and recognize shared human values alongside distinct heritages.
quiz_item.explanation: Correct Answer (A): American Cultures Requirement 1 emphasizes exploring how distinct cultural groups contribute to the nation, helping Scouts overcome stereotypes and appreciate both diversity and shared civic life.

pamphlet_excerpts: Total Cultural Isolation: What if one of the groups you are exploring had always lived alone in a city or country, with no contact with any other groups (p. 46).
Envisioning an Isolated Society: What do you think the city or country would be like today (p. 46).
Three Cultures Living Together: What would it be like if all three of your groups lived there at the same time (p. 46).
Imaginative Cultural Comparison: For requirement 2, you must stretch your imagination (p. 46).
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 - Compare Shared Community Life: What would it be like if all three of your groups lived there at the same time (p. 46).
Step 2 - Stretch Your Cultural Imagination: For requirement 2, you must stretch your imagination (p. 46).
Step 3 - Picture Life in Isolation: Picture yourself in a different cultural group and imagine what your life would be like in that society if it had always been isolated (p. 46).
Step 4 - Remove Borrowed Outside Technologies: In this situation, members of the community would have no technology borrowed from other groups, and no idea that other cultures exist (p. 46).

B. It would automatically adopt international trade laws without outside contact
C. It would speak every major world language fluently
D. It would rely entirely on imported agricultural tools

pamphlet_excerpts: Clues in Family Photographs: Old family photographs offer glimpses of the past and may provide significant clues about your own cultural background (p. 40).
Multi Country Family Origins: Many Americans can trace their origins back to several countries (p. 40).

Blended Family Heritage Traditions: It's common for an American to have a multicultural heritage, that is, to keep family traditions or customs that have been passed down from several cultures (p. 40).
Preserving Heritage Every Day: Some families know a great deal about their history and preserve their heritage in daily life (p. 40).
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 - Identify Inherited Family Customs: It's common for an American to have a multicultural heritage, that is, to keep family traditions or customs that have been passed down from several cultures (p. 40).
Step 2 - Observe Daily Heritage Practices: Some families know a great deal about their history and preserve their heritage in daily life (p. 40).
Step 3 - Research Unknown Family Backgrounds: Other families know very little about their backgrounds (p. 40).
Step 4 - Share Ancestral Findings Together: Your family may enjoy learning with you as you explore the culture of your ancestors (p. 40).

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: When comparing three different cultural groups in the United States for Requirement 1, what is the primary goal of examining their traditions, customs, and historical contributions?
patrol_quiz_bank.question: When comparing three different cultural groups in the United States for Requirement 1, what is the primary goal of examining their traditions, customs, and historical contributions?
options: A. To understand how diverse cultural backgrounds shape American society, build mutual respect, and recognize shared human values alongside distinct heritages.
B. To rank cultural groups by the century they arrived in North America and determine which group should set uniform national customs.
C. To prove that regional differences in language, food, and holidays have completely disappeared in modern metropolitan areas.
D. To replace local cultural celebrations with a single standardized set of civic traditions across all states.
choices: A. To understand how diverse cultural backgrounds shape American society, build mutual respect, and recognize shared human values alongside distinct heritages.
B. To rank cultural groups by the century they arrived in North America and determine which group should set uniform national customs.
C. To prove that regional differences in language, food, and holidays have completely disappeared in modern metropolitan areas.
D. To replace local cultural celebrations with a single standardized set of civic traditions across all states.
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: A. To understand how diverse cultural backgrounds shape American society, build mutual respect, and recognize shared human values alongside distinct heritages.
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (A): American Cultures Requirement 1 emphasizes exploring how distinct cultural groups contribute to the nation, helping Scouts overcome stereotypes and appreciate both diversity and shared civic life.
